From da6f5bbc2e7902f578b503f2a4c3d8d09ca4b102 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Deepanshu Kartikey <kartikey406@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 07:50:33 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] gfs2: fix memory leaks in gfs2_fill_super error path

Fix two memory leaks in the gfs2_fill_super() error handling path when
transitioning a filesystem to read-write mode fails.

First leak: kthread objects (thread_struct, task_struct, etc.)
When gfs2_freeze_lock_shared() fails after init_threads() succeeds, the
created kernel threads (logd and quotad) are never destroyed. This
occurs because the fail_per_node label doesn't call
gfs2_destroy_threads().

Second leak: quota bitmap buffer (8192 bytes)
When gfs2_make_fs_rw() fails after gfs2_quota_init() succeeds but
before other operations complete, the allocated quota bitmap is never
freed.

The fix moves thread cleanup to the fail_per_node label to handle all
error paths uniformly. gfs2_destroy_threads() is safe to call
unconditionally as it checks for NULL pointers. Quota cleanup is added
in gfs2_make_fs_rw() to properly handle the withdrawal case where
quota initialization succeeds but the filesystem is then withdrawn.

Thread leak backtrace (gfs2_freeze_lock_shared failure):
  unreferenced object 0xffff88801d7bca80 (size 4480):
    copy_process+0x3a1/0x4670 kernel/fork.c:2422
    kernel_clone+0xf3/0x6e0 kernel/fork.c:2779
    kthread_create_on_node+0x100/0x150 kernel/kthread.c:478
    init_threads+0xab/0x350 fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c:611
    gfs2_fill_super+0xe5c/0x1240 fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c:1265

Quota leak backtrace (gfs2_make_fs_rw failure):
  unreferenced object 0xffff88812de7c000 (size 8192):
    gfs2_quota_init+0xe5/0x820 fs/gfs2/quota.c:1409
    gfs2_make_fs_rw+0x7a/0xe0 fs/gfs2/super.c:149
    gfs2_fill_super+0xfbb/0x1240 fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c:1275

Reported-by: syzbot+aac438d7a1c44071e04b@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=aac438d7a1c44071e04b
Fixes: 6c7410f44961 ("gfs2: gfs2_freeze_lock_shared cleanup")
Fixes: b66f723bb552 ("gfs2: Improve gfs2_make_fs_rw error handling")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260131062509.77974-1-kartikey406@gmail.com/T/ [v1]
Signed-off-by: Deepanshu Kartikey <kartikey406@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Andreas Gruenbacher <agruenba@redhat.com>

diff --git a/fs/gfs2/super.c b/fs/gfs2/super.c
index f6cd907b3ec6..d96160636161 100644
--- a/fs/gfs2/super.c
+++ b/fs/gfs2/super.c
@@ -147,8 +147,10 @@ int gfs2_make_fs_rw(struct gfs2_sbd *sdp)
 	}
 
 	error = gfs2_quota_init(sdp);
-	if (!error && gfs2_withdrawn(sdp))
+	if (!error && gfs2_withdrawn(sdp)) {
+		gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp);
 		error = -EIO;
+	}
 	if (!error)
 		set_bit(SDF_JOURNAL_LIVE, &sdp->sd_flags);
 	return error;
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c b/fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c
index e7a88b717991..c7d57de7c8f0 100644
--- a/fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c
+++ b/fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c
@@ -1276,7 +1276,6 @@ static int gfs2_fill_super(struct super_block *sb, struct fs_context *fc)
 
 	if (error) {
 		gfs2_freeze_unlock(sdp);
-		gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp);
 		fs_err(sdp, "can't make FS RW: %d\n", error);
 		goto fail_per_node;
 	}
@@ -1286,6 +1285,7 @@ static int gfs2_fill_super(struct super_block *sb, struct fs_context *fc)
 
 fail_per_node:
 	init_per_node(sdp, UNDO);
+	gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp);
 fail_inodes:
 	init_inodes(sdp, UNDO);
 fail_sb:

The patch addresses two memory leaks in the `gfs2_fill_super()` error path when mounting fails after partial initialization.

**Changes in `fs/gfs2/super.c`**:
- In `gfs2_make_fs_rw()`, after a successful `gfs2_quota_init()`, if the filesystem has been withdrawn (`gfs2_withdrawn()`), the function now calls `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp)` before returning `-EIO`. This prevents leaking the allocated quota bitmap buffer (8192 bytes) when the filesystem is withdrawn before `gfs2_quota_init()` completes successfully.

**Changes in `fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c`**:
- In `gfs2_fill_super()`, the call to `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp)` was previously placed only in the error path for `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` failure. It has been removed from there and moved to the `fail_per_node` label, which is a common cleanup point after successful `init_threads()`. This ensures that if `gfs2_freeze_lock_shared()` or any later step fails (e.g., after `init_inodes` succeeded), the kernel threads (logd, quotad) created by `init_threads()` are properly destroyed.

**Relationship**: Both modifications target the same error recovery flow in `gfs2_fill_super()`. The first fixes a leak of quota resources when `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` fails due to a withdrawn filesystem. The second fixes a leak of thread objects when any operation after `init_threads()` fails (including the `gfs2_freeze_lock_shared()` call that occurs before `gfs2_make_fs_rw()`). By moving thread cleanup to the common `fail_per_node` label, the patch ensures that thread resources are freed in all error scenarios that occur after thread creation, while the quota cleanup is handled inline within `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` at the exact point where the leak could occur.

## Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes two memory leaks in the error handling path of `gfs2_fill_super()` when transitioning a GFS2 filesystem to read-write mode fails.

### Modifications in `fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c`

- **Removed** the `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp)` call from the error block that handles `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` failure (lines ~1276–1281).
- **Added** `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp)` to the `fail_per_node` label, which is reached by all error paths after `init_threads()` has succeeded. This ensures that kernel threads (logd, quotad) are always cleaned up when the filesystem mount fails, including the case where `gfs2_freeze_lock_shared()` fails after thread creation.

### Modification in `fs/gfs2/super.c`

- Inside `gfs2_make_fs_rw()`, after `gfs2_quota_init(sdp)` succeeds and the filesystem is found to be withdrawn, the quota bitmap (allocated by `gfs2_quota_init()`) is now properly freed via a call to `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp)` before returning an error (`-EIO`).

### Relationship Between the Modifications

The two changes target independent leaks that occur in different parts of the same overall error path. The `ops_fstype.c` fix addresses the leak of kernel thread structures when higher-level operations (like freezing) fail after threads are created. The `super.c` fix addresses the leak of the quota bitmap when the filesystem is withdrawn right after quota initialization succeeds. Both changes together ensure that all allocated resources (threads and quota memory) are cleaned up in the error handling sequence of `gfs2_fill_super()`.

The patch fixes two memory leaks in the error path of `gfs2_fill_super`:

1. **`fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c`: Thread leak fix**  
   - Moved `gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp)` from inside the `gfs2_make_fs_rw` error block to the `fail_per_node` label.

2. **`fs/gfs2/super.c`: Quota bitmap leak fix**  
   - Added `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp)` inside `gfs2_make_fs_rw` when `gfs2_quota_init` succeeds but the filesystem is withdrawn (returns `-EIO`).  
   - This frees the 8KB quota bitmap buffer that was allocated but not released if the filesystem becomes withdrawn immediately after quota initialization.

**Relationship**: Both leaks occur in the error handling of `gfs2_fill_super`. The first addresses a missing cleanup of thread objects; the second addresses a missing cleanup of quota memory. They are independent but collectively plug two memory leaks triggered when transitioning a filesystem to read-write mode fails.

        Root cause:
        In the error handling path of gfs2_fill_super, when gfs2_freeze_lock_shared() fails after init_threads() succeeds, kernel threads (logd, quotad) are not destroyed because gfs2_destroy_threads() was incorrectly placed only inside the gfs2_make_fs_rw error block, not at the fail_per_node label. Additionally, in gfs2_make_fs_rw, if gfs2_quota_init() succeeds but the filesystem is withdrawn, the allocated quota bitmap buffer is not freed because gfs2_quota_cleanup() is missing.
        
        Commit message:
        gfs2: fix memory leaks in gfs2_fill_super error path

Fix two memory leaks in the gfs2_fill_super() error handling path when
transitioning a filesystem to read-write mode fails.

First leak: kthread objects (thread_struct, task_struct, etc.)
When gfs2_freeze_lock_shared() fails after init_threads() succeeds, the
created kernel threads (logd and quotad) are never destroyed. This
occurs because the fail_per_node label doesn't call
gfs2_destroy_threads().

Second leak: quota bitmap buffer (8192 bytes)
When gfs2_make_fs_rw() fails after gfs2_quota_init() succeeds but
before other operations complete, the allocated quota bitmap is never
freed.

The fix moves thread cleanup to the fail_per_node label to handle all
error paths uniformly. gfs2_destroy_threads() is safe to call
unconditionally as it checks for NULL pointers. Quota cleanup is added
in gfs2_make_fs_rw() to properly handle the withdrawal case where
quota initialization succeeds but the filesystem is then withdrawn.

Thread leak backtrace (gfs2_freeze_lock_shared failure):
  unreferenced object 0xffff88801d7bca80 (size 4480):
    copy_process+0x3a1/0x4670 kernel/fork.c:2422
    kernel_clone+0xf3/0x6e0 kernel/fork.c:2779
    kthread_create_on_node+0x100/0x150 kernel/kthread.c:478
    init_threads+0xab/0x350 fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c:611
    gfs2_fill_super+0xe5c/0x1240 fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c:1265

Quota leak backtrace (gfs2_make_fs_rw failure):

    gfs2_make_fs_rw+0x7a/0xe0 fs/gfs2/super.c:149
    gfs2_fill_super+0xfbb/0x1240 fs/gfs2/ops_fstype.c:1275
